messages:
alex: Quick question — should we surface model version info to clients as human-friendly releases, or keep only opaque rollout IDs? I worry about coupling clients to our rollout cadence.
meera: +1 that concern. Exposing a stable release tag helps debugging, but if clients pin too aggressively it can kill canaries.
jon: We currently return a long 'model-stamp' in metadata. It's helpful for ops but noisy for SDKs.
sam: Proposal: split into two response headers: X-Model-Release (semantic, eg `v2.1`) and X-Model-Instance (opaque id). Clients can choose which to use.
priya: For Dedicated/Private customers they might want to pin the instance for affinity. If we expose instance IDs we need an opt-in toggle per tenant.
meera: I like two-field approach. Also need guidance for caching layers/CDNs. If CDNs cache by Release header we could accidentally pin traffic.
junior-hack: (lol) what's the harm in letting clients add Accept-Model: release=v2?
jon: The harm is coupling and unexpected caching. Also older SDKs expect `model_id` in body responses — we should preserve that mapping.
alex: Example headers idea:
```
Accept-Model: release=v2; sticky=true
X-Model-Release: v2.1
X-Model-Instance: inst-20260301-abcd
```
meera: +emoji :thinking_face: We should also add a server-side flag `expose_instance_id` so we can disable instance leaks for public hosted API. Private+Dedicated can enable.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary v2 -> 10% traffic (obs: release tag `v2.1`).
sam: Telemetry note: correlate traces using X-Model-Instance. That lets us track per-instance regressions without surfacing infra details in docs.
priya: Security/privacy: avoid putting internal cluster topology in the instance ID. Use short opaque IDs.
jon: Backcompat: SDKs released before this change should ignore unknown headers. We need a minor SDK bump to parse X-Model-Release.
meera: Docs/contract: one para describing semantics, plus the migration checklist for SDKs and CDNs. Also call out that Release tags are stable semantic identifiers, Instance IDs are ephemeral.
alex: Tradeoffs list for RFC:
- Pros of exposing Release: easier debugging, A/B by release, clearer rollout signals.
- Cons: caching/pinning risk, expands public contract, ops surface area.
- Pros of exposing Instance: fine-grained telemetry, deterministic repro.
- Cons: potential info leak, client pinning can block rollouts.
sam: Implementation sketch: add route config `expose_model_metadata: [none|release|release_and_instance]` default `release`. Update routing to respect `Accept-Model` header if present and allowed by tenant.
priya: Asked legal about data exposure; they prefer default-off for instance IDs on hosted. Private tenants can opt in.
meera: Action items: @alex draft header spec + examples, @jon draft SDK changes, @sam ops to add tenant toggle, @priya confirm opt-in wording with legal. I'll write the documentation section for caching guidance.
alex: I'll put a short PR with header names and semantics. Will ping when ready. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: noted — adding rollout-label `v2.1` to observability metadata.
jon: Quick nit — define TTL for Release tags (can they be retagged?). Recommend immutable release tags once announced.
meera: Agreed. Treat release tags as stable. If we need fixes, create `v2.1.1`.
alex: Cool. Let's sync again after PRs.
meera: Thanks all — good tradeoff call.
